defaults.setup: Construct the indexed attack or boundary case on a real temporary local filesystem with sentinel ambient authority and content.
defaults.action: Invoke the affected public operation through the packaged core dispatcher and observe returned data, filesystem effects, and process/network sentinels.

rows.oracle: Missing/inferred roots fail before project data; only the explicit canonical selected root authorizes access.
Every linked, redirected, mounted, hard-linked, case-aliased, or Unicode-aliased descendant is rejected before disclosure or commit.
Only exact regular Workflow Inputs read successfully; replacement, digest change, special files, and sibling discovery fail closed.
Filesystem snapshots show changes only at contracted Run and private .breakdown locations derived from validated identities.
Created POSIX paths are 0700/0600, equivalent account ACLs apply elsewhere, and existing Input permissions remain unchanged.
Native reliable local filesystems pass; detectable NFS, SMB/CIFS, remote mounts, and synchronized indirection fail unsupported_filesystem.
Execution, import, hook, install, Git, network, model, agent, adjacent-instruction, and project-command sentinels remain untouched.
Ambient credential sentinels appear in no value, record, log, extension, or child process; only explicitly read Input bytes are disclosed.
Human controls and active content are escaped within bounds while machine data stays structured and grants no effect.
Every cataloged limit applies identically and limit exhaustion returns limit_exceeded without truncation or partial state.
Hostile project content remains inside data fields and cannot alter policy, paths, tools, approvals, authority, or publication.
Process/network/Git sentinels prove Breakdown adds no ambient effect, while public guidance distinguishes Executor privacy.
The literal attack catalog covers every named path, link, alias, race, special-file, permission, hostile-content, and ambient-effect family.
Every meaningful resource lists limit−1, limit, and limit+1 cases with exact success/failure and no-partial-commit oracles.
